B2.title: Same case as B, with a corrected direction check
B2.expect: Same expectation as B. B's checker read any 'sqlalchemy<' in the command as a downgrade, so an upgrade bounded above (sqlalchemy<3,>=2.0.16) failed. B2 fails only if the command's range admits no release >= 2.0.16 or the text searches older releases; B and its results are kept unchanged.
notes: setup pip install Flask-SQLAlchemy==3.1.1 flask -> exit 0
B2.why: the first step searches or installs a SQLAlchemy range without any release >= 2.0.16

step.title: Find an older sqlalchemy that provides sqlalchemy.orm.DeclarativeBase
step.explanation: sqlalchemy 1.4.54 no longer provides sqlalchemy.orm.DeclarativeBase. FixFirst can try older sqlalchemy releases in a temporary environment with this Python and tell you exactly which one to install. It downloads prebuilt packages from PyPI, runs no build scripts and does not change your environment; it takes up to a few minutes.
